title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for poorly controlled diabetes.

HPI
Pt is a 77 y.o. female presenting for f/u of T2DM. Pt reports increased thirst and frequent urination over the last month. Admits to inconsistent adherence to medication regimen. Recent home glucose readings have been elevated. Pt denies any acute distress or vision changes. 

Medication List
Insulin glargine, Metformin 500mg BID, Lisinopril 10mg daily.

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Vitals: BP 132/84, HR 74, RR 16, Temp 98.6 F.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Lungs: CTAB.
Ext: WNL.

Assessment
1. T2DM: Pt presents with hyperglycemia. Current management is suboptimal.

Plan
1. Continue current insulin and oral hypoglycemic medications. 
2. Increase Metformin dosage to 850mg BID.
3. Pt to monitor fingerstick glucose 3x daily and maintain a log for review at next visit.
4. F/u in 4 weeks.

Electronically signed, 
L. Moreau, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
